rationale: The plan correctly consumes the existing DESeq2 table without refitting, ranks all 12,000 genes by the Wald statistic (fallback signed -log10 p) with explicit tie and non-finite rules, and runs gseapy prerank against a named local Hallmark GMT (v2026.1) with a 15-500 size window, reporting NES, nominal p, and FDR q with directional interpretation and a shallow-sample caveat. It falls short of the reference by not fixing the permutation count (>=1000) or a random seed, and by not reporting the leading-edge genes per set; the added ORA on padj<0.05 lists is framed as a secondary cross-check rather than the answer, which is tolerable but adds a method the reference considers uninformative here. The DE-pipeline criteria (QC, filtering, normalization, formula, shrinkage) are largely moot for an enrichment-only task; the plan states the contrast direction, BH thresholds, and a policy of flagging rather than re-estimating sample_01, but does no sample-structure QC and does not address counts versus tested-gene filtering beyond keeping the full list.
